verses.text: Very early in the morning, the chief priests, the elders, the teachers of the law and the whole Council made their plans. They tied up Jesus, led him away and handed him over to Pilate.
"Are you the king of the Jews?" asked Pilate. "You have said so," Jesus replied.
The chief priests accused him of many things.
So Pilate asked him again, "Are you not going to answer? Look how many things they are accusing you of."
But Jesus still did not answer, and Pilate was amazed.
It was the custom at the feast to set free one prisoner, whoever the people asked for.
A man called Barabbas was in prison with some others who had fought against the rulers. They had committed murder during the fighting.
The crowd came up and asked Pilate to do for them what he usually did.
"Do you want me to set the king of the Jews free for you?" asked Pilate.
He knew that the chief priests had handed Jesus over to him because they were jealous.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to ask Pilate to set Barabbas free instead.
"Then what should I do with the one you call the king of the Jews?" Pilate asked them.
"Nail him to a cross!" they shouted.
"Why? What wrong has he done?" asked Pilate. But they shouted even louder, "Nail him to a cross!"
Pilate wanted to please the crowd. So he set Barabbas free for them. He had Jesus whipped, and then he handed him over to be nailed to a cross.
The soldiers led Jesus away into the courtyard of the palace, called the Praetorium. They called together the whole company of soldiers.
They put a purple robe on him. Then they twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on his head.
And they began to call out to him, "Hail, king of the Jews!"
Again and again they hit him on the head with a stick and spat on him. They fell on their knees and pretended to worship him.
After they had made fun of him, they took off the purple robe and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led him out to nail him to a cross.
A man named Simon, from Cyrene, was passing by on his way in from the country. He was the father of Alexander and Rufus. The soldiers forced him to carry the cross.
They brought Jesus to the place called Golgotha, which means the Place of the Skull.
Then they offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not drink it.
They nailed him to the cross. They divided up his clothes by throwing dice to see what each one would get.
It was nine o'clock in the morning when they nailed him to the cross.
A notice was put up saying why he was being punished. It read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
They nailed two robbers to crosses with him, one on his right and one on his left.
So the Scripture came true that says, "He was counted among the people who broke the law."
People who passed by shouted insults at him. They shook their heads and said, "So! You who are going to destroy the temple and build it again in three days,
come down from the cross and save yourself!"
In the same way, the chief priests and the teachers of the law made fun of him among themselves. "He saved others," they said, "but he cannot save himself!
Let this Christ, this king of Israel, come down now from the cross! When we see that, we will believe." Those who were nailed to crosses with him also insulted him.
At twelve o'clock, darkness covered the whole land until three o'clock in the afternoon.
At three o'clock Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?" This means, "My God, my God, why have you left me all alone?"
Some of the people standing nearby heard this. They said, "Listen! He is calling for Elijah."
Someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a stick and offered it to Jesus to drink. "Leave him alone," he said. "Let us see if Elijah comes to take him down."
Then Jesus cried out with a loud voice and took his last breath.
The curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
A Roman officer was standing there in front of Jesus. He heard his cry and saw how he died. Then he said, "This man really was the Son of God!"
Some women were watching from far away. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
In Galilee these women had followed Jesus and taken care of him. Many other women were there too. They had come up with him to Jerusalem.
It was the day of preparation, the day before the Sabbath. So as evening came,
Joseph from Arimathea went boldly to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body. Joseph was an important member of the Council, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God.
Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead. He called the Roman officer and asked him if Jesus had already died.
When the officer told him it was true, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.
So Joseph bought some linen cloth. He took down the body and wrapped it in the linen. Then he placed it in a tomb cut out of rock. He rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where Jesus was laid.
